meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/03, Thursday 15 May 2025). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: 100 marks, read from the [N] part markers in the QP margin. q16-q18 and q23-q26 reappear on J560/06 (Higher) with identical marks and identical tags.

coding_notes: q1 (name a chord, name the circumference, draw a diameter) tagged parts_of_a_circle — that node's own example is naming a chord, and it costs no prerequisites.

q8a ('think of a number', subtract then divide) tagged function_machines rather than solving_linear_equations: the mark scheme's first route is inverse operations, and function_machines credits only simple_arithmetic where solving_linear_equations credits four.
q9 (currency conversion against a budget) tagged proportion — the exchange rate is a multiplier, and no currency-conversion node exists.

q10b (find another pair of values for a two-step machine with a fixed output) tagged function_machines + factors_and_multiples: the machine is subtract-then-multiply, so the second value must divide the fixed output.

q15b (why one correct area-of-a-circle answer can exceed another) tagged area_of_a_circle + rounding — the whole point is the accuracy of the value used for pi, which is a rounding judgement, and the taxonomy has no node for it.
q18b (why a graph with a truncated vertical axis is misleading) tagged simple_charts: criticising a chart's scale sits inside reading charts, and there is no misleading-graphs node.

q19 (similar cuboids, height from base areas) tagged congruence_and_similarity. This is the taxonomy's known 'similar solids' gap noted in docs/coding-a-paper.md — area and volume scale factors have no node of their own — and it is a poor fit carrying 4 marks.
q7 (weekly pay to hourly pay) tagged simple_arithmetic: it is two successive divisions, and compound_units would over-claim a rates skill the question never tests.
